extracted.intended_audience: International Preliminary Examining Authority examiners, national/regional patent examiners and applicants/agents involved in PCT Chapter II proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for processing Chapter II PCT demands: when to issue written opinions, how to handle amendments, rectifications, interviews/top‑up searches, timing and establishment of the international preliminary examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for not preparing a written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same Authority is both International Searching Authority and International Preliminary Examining Authority and a demand has been filed before the ISA written opinion is prepared, no written opinion is required if criteria (i)–(vi) are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) the claimed invention satisfies Article 33(1) (novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability); (ii) the application complies with PCT form and contents requirements; (iii) the application meets requirements on clarity of claims, description and drawings and claims are fully supported by the description as in Article 35(2) and Rule 70.12(ii) or the examiner does not wish to make observations (Rule 66.2(a)(v)); (iv) no amendment goes beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed; (v) all claims relate to an invention for which an ISR is being established and an IPEA report will be established for all claims; (vi) where applicable, a nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing is available in a form permitting meaningful IPE.  Also applies where the ISA written opinion is treated as the IPEA first written opinion; in that case the examiner takes into account applicant comments/amendments when establishing the IPEA report.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a further written opinion may be issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances in which the IPEA may, at its discretion, issue one or more additional written opinions after the first written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A further written opinion may be issued if the applicant made a credible attempt to overcome/rebut objections but failed to satisfy the examiner and there is sufficient time to establish the IPEA report within the Rule 69.2 limit. A further written opinion should be issued when a top‑up search yields prior art on which new objections will be raised. The examiner may issue additional written opinions if doing so would facilitate resolution of significant issues, provided time remains, the applicant is making a real effort to meet objections, and the Authority has resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle to minimize number of written opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should be guided by the overriding principle that an international preliminary examination report should be established after as few written opinions as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control the procedure with this principle in mind; repeat communications only if helpful. If applicant is not making a real effort to address objections (by amendments or counter‑arguments), the examiner should, at the conclusion of the first or second written opinion stage, establish the IPEA report. If new objections arise from a top‑up search, issue a second written opinion to notify the applicant. Consider whether issues are best resolved by further written opinion, telephone discussion, or interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: claims without an international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: International preliminary examination can be carried out only on inventions for which the International Searching Authority has established an international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Article 33(6): the IPEA must take into consideration documents cited in the international search report. Claims for inventions without an ISR need not be subject to IPE. (See paragraph 10.73 for exceptions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal standard of examination at all stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should apply the same standard of international preliminary examination in relation to matters of substance at all stages of processing the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the ISA has established a first written opinion, the examiner need not completely re‑read an amended application if the first opinion was comprehensive; concentrate on the amendments themselves, related passages, and deficiencies indicated in the first opinion (see paragraph 17.55).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inviting replies and opportunities for amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing additional written opinions, the examiner should invite the applicant to submit a written reply and, where appropriate, amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receipt of an additional opinion, applicant may amend claims/description/drawings or submit arguments or both. Conditions for amendments as set out in paragraphs 20.04–20.22 apply. The examiner may give one or more additional opportunities to submit amendments or arguments if necessary and time allows (see paragraphs 19.10 and 19.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of written opinions on arguments-only responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a response to a written opinion is received as arguments only, the written opinion is reconsidered in light of those arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the response includes amendments (other than rectification of obvious mistakes), the amended parts are considered under the amendment rules (paragraphs 20.04–20.22). The IPEA report should indicate that applicant’s arguments were taken into account and the examiner should comment on relevant applicant arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling late responses after time limit expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: If the time limit for response to a further written opinion expires without response, the file is forwarded to the examiner who prepared the opinion to establish the IPEA report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a response is received after the time limit but before the report is established, the response can be considered; however Rule 66.4bis states that amendments, arguments or rectifications of obvious mistakes need not be taken into account. See paragraph 20.05 for guidance on late submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction (re‑opening) of the IPEA report
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA may establish a corrected international preliminary examination report in exceptional circumstances after a report has been issued, where circumstances justify such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected/replacement report should be clearly labelled so elected Offices are aware. Retraction will not be done merely because applicant disagrees. Re‑opening justified where report was issued earlier than it should have been due to error/omission by the IPEA (e.g., omission of a timely filed amendment). Once re‑opened, subsequent requests to re‑open that application should not be entertained. The International Bureau must be advised to disregard the earlier report. If resulting response is a further written opinion, it is sent only to applicant; if a corrected IPEA report, it is sent to applicant and International Bureau as a 'corrected version'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes obviously not as intended (linguistic, spelling errors, etc.) may be rectified if a request is submitted within 26 months from the priority date; rectification cannot be made for substantive changes like cancellation of claims or omission of passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to authorization (Rule 91.1(d)), rectification can be requested by applicant or noted by examiner. The Authority may authorize rectification in parts of the application other than the request, but only if requested within 26 months from priority. A rectification authorized under Rule 91.1 shall be taken into account by the IPEA for the purposes of IPE, but need not be taken into account for the written opinion or IPEA report if received/authorized/notified after the Authority has begun to draw up that opinion or report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal communication with the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA may at any time communicate informally (telephone, writing, interviews) with the applicant or agent; interviews are discretionary and may be granted if useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications are usually with the applicant’s agent. When arranging an interview, the matters for discussion should be stated and recorded. Recording depends on matters' gravity: for minor clarifications, a brief file note is usually sufficient; for substantive issues (novelty, inventive step, new‑matter), a fuller note may be made (optionally using Forms PCT/IPEA/428 and PCT/IPEA/429) and a copy may be sent to applicant. If new substantive objections are raised at interview and not agreed upon, confirm in additional written opinion inviting response within prescribed time. Telephone discussions should be documented on file including any agreements reached. Records should indicate whether a response is due or whether the examiner will issue another written opinion or establish the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and content limits of the IPEA report
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA report should be issued within the prescribed time limit; it follows written opinions and communications and must not contain any statement on national patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments, arguments and requests for rectification of obvious mistakes submitted before the examiner has begun to draw up the report must be taken into account. Amendments/arguments/requests received after drafting began need not be considered. The report is prepared on Form PCT/IPEA/409 and should avoid statements about whether the claimed invention is or seems to be patentable/unpatentable under national law. Chapter 17 provides detailed guidance on completing the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and calculation of applicable time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Authority determines applicable time limits, the examiner must consult all relevant factors and PCT Regulations governing such time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include translations of priority documents, amendments, rectifications, response to first written opinion, restricting claims/payment of fees, furnishing priority documents, and establishment of the IPEA report. Time limits are usually specified in full months, calculated from the day after mailing of communication. Rules cover contingencies (office closed, official holidays), disruptions in postal service, excuse of delays for force majeure or unavailability of electronic means, and extension of time limits in case of general disruption affecting the Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of applicant's failure to respond within time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not respond within a prescribed time limit, the effect differs by circumstances; the IPEA may proceed in various ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA report may be established as if priority had not been claimed, established on the 'main invention', or established with a negative determination. Normally, amendments, arguments and rectifications received after the examiner has begun to draw up the opinion/report need not be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of the demand or all elections
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant withdraws the demand or all elections by signed notice sent to the International Bureau, the IPEA is notified and processing is discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of withdrawal must be signed by all applicants of record or the agent provided a power of attorney signed by all applicants has been filed; the requirement for an agent to have a power of attorney cannot be waived for withdrawal. If the notice of withdrawal is submitted to the IPEA, it marks the date of receipt and transmits it promptly to the International Bureau; the notice is considered submitted to the IB on the date marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 19 amendments prior to IPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments of the claims filed under Article 19 (prior to start of IPE) must not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed and will be transmitted to the IPEA by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a demand for IPE has been submitted, the applicant should preferably file a copy of Article 19 amendments and the Rule 46.5(b) letter with the IPEA. If the time limit for filing Article 19 amendments has not expired and the demand includes a statement postponing start of IPE, the IPE should not start before: (a) examiner receives a copy of Article 19 amendments; or (b) applicant gives notice they do not wish to make Article 19 amendments; or (c) the later of two months from transmittal of the international search report or 16 months from priority date. Article 19 amendments are considered only during the international preliminary examination procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments under Article 34 / Rule 66.8
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the description, claims or drawings during IPE are made under Rule 66.8; applicant is not restricted to amendments necessary to remedy defects but amendments must not add subject matter or render the application objectionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be submitted to avoid objections of lack of novelty/inventive step in view of ISR citations or other objections. Any amendment submitted must not add subject matter beyond the disclosure as originally filed and must not introduce obscurity. See paragraphs 20.10–20.19 for added‑matter guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and formal requirements for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change (other than rectification of obvious mistakes) to claims, description or drawings is an amendment; amendments must be submitted in the language of IPE and follow specified form requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to description/drawings must be made by filing replacement sheets when they differ; amendments to claims must be filed as a complete set replacing all claims originally filed or previously amended (Articles 19/34). Replacement sheets must be accompanied by a letter drawing attention to differences, indicating basis in application as filed and preferably explaining reasons. Cancellation of entire sheets must be by letter. Replacement sheets/sets of claims must be in typed form, though handwritten amendments may be allowed at examiner's discretion. Minor corrections (e.g., ≤6 words) may be accepted as interlineations on a typescript if clean; examiners should invite resubmission in proper form when principles are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraisal of amendments — examiner checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner ensures amendments do not add content beyond the application as filed and do not make the amended application objectionable under the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable amendments include restrictions of scope, improvements of clarity, or claim amendments desirable without changing subject matter. An amended application must satisfy all PCT requirements. When claims have been substantially limited, examiner should pay special attention to: (i) unity of invention (do amended claims satisfy Rule 13?), (ii) agreement of description and claims (do embodiments remain within claim scope; may require description amendment; check title appropriateness), (iii) support — are all amended claims supported by the description (see paragraphs 5.43–5.44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Added subject‑matter: test for going beyond the disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment introduces subject matter extending beyond the content of the application as filed if the overall change results in the skilled person being presented with information not expressly or inherently presented in the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherency requires that the missing descriptive matter is necessarily present and would be recognized by the person skilled in the art; probabilities/possibilities are insufficient. Examples: introducing a further ingredient or specifying a previously unspecified kind of resilient support (e.g., helical springs) is normally beyond the disclosure unless the skilled person would necessarily understand it (see paragraph 20.14). Replacement sheets containing added subject matter are indicated in the IPEA report and attached with accompanying letters (Rule 70.16(a)); such amendments are treated as not considered for purposes of the IPEA report but are included as filed and marked 'SUPERSEDED REPLACEMENT SHEET' where applicable. Later‑filed examples or statements of advantage should be treated with caution as they may prima facie extend disclosure; clarifications of effects clearly deducible by the skilled person may be permissible.
